canonical_title: Ground burst, air burst, and gun ricochet

versions.title_at_revision: Ground burst, air burst, and gun ricochet
versions.text:
Standard: The safe release envelope (e.g., safe release altitude, safe release airspeed) is defined such that releasing or employing a store will ensure the air vehicle is not critically damaged by weapon fragmentation resulting from intended downrange detonation. Ricochet from gunfire operations do not have the potential to strike the air vehicle within the safe firing envelope. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Determine the threshold for Ph to launch air vehicle from fragmentation effects (ground fragmentation, terrain, and air burst fragmentation separately) that would result in critical damage to the air vehicle.
(2) Establish the minimum fuze arm time required to achieve safe escape.
(3) Conduct SEA by modeling the air vehicle, weapon, and fragment trajectories that include the point of detonation. Burst analyses determine if an air vehicle can safely release a weapon with a fuze that functions properly, (e.g., that detonates on the ground or target (impact fuze) or at a HAT or distance to target (proximity fuze). The Ph by fragmentation to the air vehicle is modeled considering factors such as the air vehicle release conditions and flight path, the weapon’s trajectory and orientation after launch, the warhead’s fragmentation data informed by static arena testing, and if applicable, fuze reliability data, specifically fuze failure rate. Types of burst analyses to be conducted: a. Fragment minimum altitude: The lowest altitude or target separation distance where the risk to the air vehicle due to fragments from ground weapon detonations does not exceed the risk criteria. b. Terrain minimum altitude: The lowest altitude that an air vehicle can release a weapon and avoid impact with the terrain (ground and terrain clearance factor). c. Ricochet minimum altitude: The lowest open fire/cease fire altitude where air vehicle is safe from gun round ricochet or fragmentation.
(4) Evaluate the probability that a warhead or gun fragment (where applicable) can impact the delivery air vehicle upon detonation on the ground or air target (impact fuze) or at a HAT or distance to target (proximity fuze).
(5) Evaluate the probability that the delivery air vehicle will impact the terrain during weapon delivery or recovery.
(6) Identify the set of flight conditions (altitude, speed and engagement range) that will provide the air vehicle protection from the munition debris detonation at the target area given normal munition functions. This set of flight conditions, at a minimum, should include the planned flight test and release points as part of the live fire testing. Ideally, the considered envelope should characterize the entire employment envelope and weapon flight modes and fuze arm times.
(7) In cases where the Ph does not meet minimum safe escape criteria, determining Pk of the launch air vehicle may be conducted and correlated to the damage tolerance of the air vehicle to determine an overall risk. Probability of kill is determined through modeling the vulnerable areas of the launch air vehicle obtained from vulnerability analyses. Test.
  (1) Ground test: Conduct static arena test with production representative warhead to characterize the warhead fragmentation pattern, fragment size, fragment travel velocity, and fragment travel distance. Static arena test data will inform the SEA.
  (2) Flight test: Conduct instrumented live fire flight testing to verify weapon flyout behavior, validate weapon flyout models, and measure fuze arm time and reliability prior to testing with a live AUR. Live fire flight testing may inform safe and arm device reliability in order to update reliability and failure probability assessment. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Examination.
    (1) Verify that the safe release envelope necessary to maintain safe escape for store employment is defined and is accessible to flight crew (e.g., safe escape tables in weapon delivery procedures, safe escape tools in mission planning). Analysis.
(8) Determine if there is protection to prevent critical damage to the air vehicle from the munition ricochet/fragmentation and detonation effects given a downrange detonated munition.
(9) Complete SEA for the entire flight envelope (flight maneuvers, weapon flight modes, and fuze arm times) or conduct a tailored SEA for a subset of conditions that were not previously analyzed prior to flight test. Use the SEA to identify safe and unsafe employment conditions and subsequent escape maneuvers.
